documents.title: Wakapi API Reference
documents.description: A navigable Sourcey-generated reference for the Wakapi REST API, built from the project's own OpenAPI spec.
documents.searchText: # wakapi api reference {#wakapi-api-reference} is a minimalist, self-hosted, wakatime-compatible backend for coding statistics ([wakapi.dev](https://wakapi.dev), [github.com/muety/wakapi](https://github.com/muety/wakapi), mit licensed). this site generated the rest api: 22 operations across summaries, heartbeats, projects, statistics, leaders, badges, and diagnostics. it was built with [sourcey](https://sourcey.com) from openapi spec shipped in repository itself (`static/docs/swagger.yaml`), pinned to commit [`c561bbc174d139d2d3f8ee222ca61671cdc3caf1`](https://github.com/muety/wakapi/commit/c561bbc174d139d2d3f8ee222ca61671cdc3caf1) (2026-11-08). ## why exists {#why-this-exists} wakapi's documented today only as raw swagger file inside ui served by running instance. there no public, linkable user or integrator can read without server first. closes that gap: every endpoint, parameter, schema spec, one navigable place. what covered {#what-is-covered} - **summaries** — per-user status bar, ranges, all-time views **heartbeats** native heartbeat ingestion (single bulk) **projects, leaders** filtered project lists, stats leaderboards **badges diagnostics** shields.io-compatible badge data, plugin error reports **health** application health start [authentication](/wakapi-api-docs/authentication.html) `authorization` header, then [sending heartbeats](/wakapi-api-docs/heartbeats.html) worked `curl` example. full endpoint list under **api reference**.

documents.title: Authentication
documents.description: How to authenticate against the Wakapi API with an API key.
documents.searchText: # authentication {#authentication} all authenticated endpoints take an api key in the `authorization` header. is your wakapi key, base64-encoded and prefixed with `basic` (as documented spec itself): ```http authorization: basic <base64-of-your-api-key> ``` example from spec: ody2ndhknzqtmtljns00ntjilwjhmdetzmizzwm3mgq0yzjmcg== get instance: log in, open profile/settings page, copy shown there. keys are per user; keep yours private never commit it. under `/compat/wakatime/v1/` follow wakatime shape accept same shields badge endpoint (`/compat/shields/v1/{user}/{interval}/{filter}`) needs user to have public data access enabled instead of a key.

documents.title: Sending heartbeats
documents.description: A worked example of pushing a coding heartbeat to Wakapi.
documents.searchText: # sending heartbeats {#sending-heartbeats} a heartbeat records one coding event: file you edited, in project, at time. send it with `post /heartbeat`: ```bash curl -x post https://your-wakapi-instance/api/heartbeat \ -h "authorization: basic <base64-of-your-api-key>" "content-type: application/json" -d '{ "entity": "/home/user/projects/my-app/src/main.go", "type": "file", "category": "coding", "time": 1794216000, "project": "my-app", "branch": "main", "language": "go", "is_write": true }' ``` notes: - `entity` is the path, `type` usually `file`, `category` `coding`, and `time` unix timestamp. to many once, use /heartbeats` json array of same objects. wakatime-compatible clients can point `/compat/wakatime/v1/users/{user}/heartbeats` endpoints instead — payload shape, paths. native `/heartbeat` compat overlap; prefer for new integrations only when an existing wakatime client needs them. check result `get /summary` or /users/{user}/statusbar/today`.
